new_entities.name: Topical benzoyl peroxide
new_entities.description: Topically applied benzoyl peroxide formulations used to treat acne vulgaris.

new_entities.name: Clinical moderate acne
new_entities.description: Clinically assessed mild-to-moderate or moderate acne vulgaris severity and lesion burden.

edges.effect_quant: A 2021 network meta-analysis found benzoyl peroxide improved self-reported acne outcomes in about 35% of patients versus 26% with vehicle, and broader 2022 acne network evidence across roughly 35,000 observations continued to rank benzoyl peroxide-containing topical therapy as clinically effective.
edges.population: adolescents and adults with mild-to-moderate or moderate acne vulgaris treated with topical benzoyl peroxide formulations
edges.mechanism: Benzoyl peroxide reduces Cutibacterium acnes burden and exerts comedolytic and anti-inflammatory effects, which is why it remains a basic first-line topical therapy despite irritation tradeoffs.
edges.summary: Topical benzoyl peroxide remains one of the most evidence-backed acne treatments. It is not the most glamorous option, but large review-level evidence still shows real clinical improvement for mild-to-moderate inflammatory acne.
edges.caveats: Irritation, bleaching, and tolerability issues matter, and combination regimens often outperform benzoyl peroxide alone. This edge is about clinical acne improvement, not perfect clearance.

evidence.citation: ZaengleinAL et al 2020 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
StuartB et al 2021 Br J Dermatol
evidence.notes: Topical preparations for the treatment of mild-to-moderate acne vulgaris: systematic review and network meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: self-reported acne improvement with benzoyl peroxide versus 26% with vehicle

evidence.citation: SutariaAH et al 2022 Br J Dermatol
evidence.notes: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of topical pharmacological, oral pharmacological, physical and combined treatments for acne vulgaris.
